title: The Duty of Responsibility and Reasonable Steps
summary: What the duty of responsibility means in practice, how reasonable steps are judged, and the factors an authority weighs when deciding whether a senior manager fell short.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: What the duty of responsibility means in practice, how reasonable steps are judged, and the factors an authority weighs when deciding whether a senior manager fell short.
Learning Objectives: Explain the duty of responsibility and the reasonable steps test
Identify the factors used to judge whether steps were reasonable
Apply the test to realistic scenarios involving failures in the senior manager's area
Syllabus: The duty of responsibility: scope, burden and consequences
What counts as reasonable: knowledge, resources, urgency and hindsight
Acting on red flags, escalation and seeking expert advice
Scenario exercise: did the senior manager take reasonable steps
Intended Audience: Executive directors, senior managers and heads of business lines holding senior manager functions
Heads of compliance, risk, internal audit and other control functions with personal accountability
Company secretaries, HR and compliance staff who administer the accountability regime
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some management experience in a regulated firm is helpful. No legal background is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
Group of Thirty, Banking Conduct and Culture: A Call for Sustained and Comprehensive Reform (2015)
Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)
